evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.111: quae gustēmus, olfaciāmus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: As in English, also to smell out, get wind of something (Ter.; Cic.; Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: sniff at; scent, smell out (as a dog does)
evidence: Plaut. Men. 1.2.55: pallam; Hor. Epod. 6.10: cibum (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: quod tū cum olfaciēs, deōs rogābis, tōtum ut tē faciant, Fabulle, nāsum.
phrases.english: when you smell it, Fabullus, you’ll ask the gods to make you all nose.
The nose smells scents and stinks.

sources: Lewis & Short: olfacio · Lewis & Short: odoror
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-catullus, loci-comenius), checked against the editions named there.
